about: The canonical merge of every source of truth about the playbook's 36 SOTA techniques. One row per technique: what is real, what is not, the file AND symbol that implements it, the measured number or the honest reason there is none, and the playbook section.
rules: No number on this board is typed by hand. Each is read out of a generated artefact named in `provenance`, or it is absent and `no_metric_reason` says why.
A row may not claim real-* unless every code reference resolves: the file exists and the symbol is DEFINED in it. build_coverage.py exits 1 otherwise.
Null and negative results carry the same weight as positive ones and are flagged, not buried.
`not_run.est_cost_usd` is a STRING carrying arithmetic, copied verbatim from training/NOT_RUN_HERE.json. It is deliberately not a number: no one measured it.

statuses.real-measured: implemented here AND a number was measured on this machine, with provenance.
statuses.real-no-metric: implemented here and it runs, but no number is claimed - the reason is stated.
statuses.script-ready-not-executed: the script and cloud job spec exist; NO GPU, so it was never run.

techniques.name: Model-based data selection

code.note: coverage - lambda * redundancy over bge-small embeddings

techniques.headline: At the same 40% keep fraction a uniformly random subset scores 0.4228 against the selector's 0.3736 - the selector is WORSE than random by 0.0492 NDCG@10.
techniques.verdict: negative result: the random baseline BEAT the model-based selector
caveats: Dropping catalogue rows removes relevant documents, so some NDCG loss is arithmetically unavoidable. The honest question is how the selected subset compares with a random subset of the SAME size, which is why the random arm is reported alongside, together with each arm's relevant_doc_retention.

In ESCI every graded label is bound to one product_id, so a dropped relevant document cannot be substituted by a near-twin and NDCG under index pruning tracks relevant_doc_retention almost mechanically. Uniform random pruning retains exactly keep_frac of EVERY query's relevant set; a model-based scorer can only beat it by predicting which documents will be judged relevant for unseen queries. Compare the arms' relevant_doc_retention against keep_frac=0.4 to see how much signal each strategy actually carries.

techniques.name: Hybrid search + rerank
techniques.headline: The spine of the demo and the only technique with a clear positive: rerank lifts NDCG@10 from 0.5431 (bm25) to 0.6027 on 200 held-out ESCI test queries.
caveats: A laptop CPU cross-encoder. p95 sits near the 150 ms gate threshold; CPU contention alone can fail the gate.

techniques.name: Contextual retrieval
techniques.headline: NULL RESULT. On the production path the enriched index is worth -0.00015 NDCG@10, CI95 [-0.00812, 0.00795] - straddles zero. The playbook's own 'When NOT to use' names structured catalogue records; this is one.
provenance: services/search-svc/SOTA_MEASURED.json (scripts/measure_techniques.py); endpoints: scripts/contextual_enrich.py, engine.VariantIndex / Engine.rank_variant, POST /search/variant, POST /eval/contextual
techniques.verdict: null result: the 95% CI of the paired delta straddles zero
caveats: Only the enriched slice differs between the arms; every other document keeps its baseline text.
The cross-encoder pair text is unchanged, so enrichment can only move which documents reach the rerank window and in what first-stage order.
The slice is the baseline candidate pool, so a document that ONLY enrichment would have surfaced was never enriched. That makes the measurement conservative, not optimistic.
The playbook's own 'When NOT to use' for this technique names structured catalogue records. This is a structured catalogue.

techniques.name: ColPali visual retrieval
techniques.headline: NULL RESULT, and it BREACHES THE GATE. The quality delta is -0.01315 with CI95 [-0.03164, 0.00427] (straddles zero), while p95 is 181.5 ms against the demo's own 150 ms p95 release gate. No quality gain, and it would fail the gate on latency.
provenance: services/search-svc/SOTA_MEASURED.json (scripts/measure_techniques.py); endpoints: engine.Engine.maxsim / Engine.late_interaction, POST /search/late_interaction, POST /eval/late_interaction
techniques.verdict: null result: the 95% CI of the paired delta straddles zero
caveats: bge-small token vectors were trained for mean-pooled sentence similarity, not for late interaction. A trained ColBERT checkpoint has [Q]/[D] marker tokens and a learned 128-d projection this does not. This measures the SHAPE of the technique on the existing encoder, not ColBERTv2's published quality.
Latency was measured on one macOS laptop with OMP_NUM_THREADS=1, single request at a time. It is a relative comparison between arms on identical hardware, not a service SLO.

SCOPE: the playbook's technique 9 is ColPali VISUAL retrieval. What was built and measured here is the late-interaction MaxSim mechanism over TEXT on the existing bge-small encoder. The VISION variant, and a trained ColBERT checkpoint with [Q]/[D] markers and a learned projection, are ABSENT from this repo.

techniques.name: GraphRAG (routed)
techniques.headline: Router and traversal both work on the intents they were written for. The single false positive is a deliberate lexical trap ('car seat that FITS a newborn'), which is the documented failure mode of a rules-first router and the reason the playbook pairs it with a classifier fallback.
provenance: services/search-svc/SOTA_MEASURED.json (scripts/measure_techniques.py); endpoints: services/search-svc/graph.py, services/search-svc/graph_eval_set.json, GET /graph/stats, POST /graph/route, GET /graph/eval
techniques.verdict: Router and traversal both work on the intents they were written for. The single false positive is a deliberate lexical trap ('car seat that FITS a newborn'), which is the documented failure mode of a rules-first router and the reason the playbook pairs it with a classifier fallback.
caveats: n=30. A 95% Wilson interval on a proportion measured on 30 items is roughly +/-0.15-0.20 wide, so precision/recall here cannot separate a good router from a mediocre one.

Single labeller, no adjudication, no inter-annotator agreement. The labeller also wrote the router rules, so the set is not independent of the system under test - it is a smoke test, not an unbiased benchmark.
Queries are written in clean English. Real Sparky traffic is short, misspelt and elliptical, which is the regime rules routers fail in.
The hybrid half is deliberately seeded with near-miss lexical traps ('substitute' as a food word, 'fits' as a size word) because those are the cases a keyword router gets wrong.

n=30 hand-labelled queries. A 95% Wilson interval on a proportion at this sample size is roughly +/-0.15-0.20 wide, so these numbers are a smoke test of the routing rules, not evidence of generalisation.

The graph's substitute/complement/co_intent edges are derived from the SAME ESCI relevance labels the NDCG eval scores against. No graph-vs-hybrid NDCG number is reported, because it would be circular.
The router rules were debugged against this same 30-query set, so these numbers are in-sample.

a lexical judge cannot see semantics; it will call a correct substitute irrelevant. Its measured agreement with ESCI gold below is the honest ceiling on what it can tell you.

the lexical online judge does NOT agree with ESCI gold beyond chance at this sample size - a negative kappa with a relevant base rate above 70% means a judge that always said 'relevant' would score higher. The judge is not fit to gate anything and is reported as such.

slice_report.metric: engine.ndcg10 (exponential gain, @10); query selection engine.eval_qids (test split, max gain > 0)

rules.rule: starts with a question word (how/what/why/can/does/is/...) or ends with '?'
a token mixing letters+digits (not a number+unit like 20oz/144hz, not an ordinal) or a bare 4+ digit run not followed by a unit
a known acronym token (usb, hdmi, led, spf, bpa, ...) or a symbol (& + # % $ / " ')
>=1 number+unit (20 ounce, 144 hz, 8 panel, 2 pack) or >=2 colour/material/size/style words
1-2 tokens and no rule above fired
fallback (typically brand + product or 3+ word descriptive queries)

worst_slice.criterion: lowest rrf_rerank mean NDCG@10 among slices with n >= 30

fix.description: Purpose-clause-aware lexical query for use_case queries: the BM25 leg gets a rewritten query built from the product head phrase (text before 'for ...', gift/idea words removed); dense retrieval and the cross-encoder keep the original query. Gated on query_types.classify == 'use_case'; variant selected on the dev split.

tuning.selection: highest mean NDCG@10 on dev slice

non_target_queries.note: fix is gated on the classifier; non-target queries were re-run through the fix path

caveats: The query-type classifier is a hand-written rule set; it has NOT been validated against human labels and its precision/recall per class is unknown. Rules were written after eyeballing class samples of the test and dev query strings (no relevance labels were used).
Slices are imbalanced; small slices (e.g. compatibility, non_product) have wide CIs or are empty.
CIs are percentile bootstraps over queries only; they ignore uncertainty in the ESCI judgments.
Worst slice was chosen on the test set, so the choice of slice is test-informed; the fix itself uses no test labels (see fix.tuning).
Paired-delta bootstraps for different slices are computed independently; no multiple-comparison correction.
